FR-020.title: Every quantity total names its unit

FR-023.title: Weight and quantity are never compared against each other

FR-026.title: The mix panel shows the app split beside the ERP split over the same five categories

FR-028.title: Both sides of a comparison are requested with identical dates and filters

FR-029.title: ERP categories with no app counterpart appear as their own segments

FR-033.title: Infor Visual stays read only and its connection opens with read-only intent

FR-035.title: The number of receipts with no load number is disclosed

decisions.decision: On-time target is 95 per cent, held as an administrator-editable setting rather than in code
decisions.why: The spec's working default becomes deterministic, and FR-014's no-rebuild requirement is met by the existing Settings.Core mechanism and its manifest entry
decisions.rejected: Leaving it deferred to clarify, or a 95 constant in the view model, or appsettings.json which needs a file edit and a restart

decisions.decision: Coverage counts one app label against one ERP receipt line, grouped by received date and normalised category, with ERP-only categories counting toward the ERP line
decisions.why: The spec left the comparison unit unstated, and an unstated unit is how the coverage and mix panels would silently disagree with the ERP
decisions.rejected: Comparing quantities across the two systems, which cannot be done without resolving units

decisions.decision: A new IService_Tool_ReceivingAnalyticsApp, Dao_Tool_ReceivingAnalyticsApp and four stored procedures, leaving the ERP service untouched
decisions.why: The existing service depends only on IService_InforVisual; giving it a MySQL dependency hands the ERP tab a data source it never uses
decisions.rejected: Adding app methods to the existing service, or reading through IService_MySQL_Receiving which is the workflow surface not a reporting one

decisions.decision: The ERP tab markup is wrapped in a TabViewItem rather than extracted into its own control
decisions.why: Nothing moves, so the SC-008 regression risk is limited to runtime behaviour, and one view model per tab makes cross-tab filter leakage structurally impossible
decisions.rejected: Extracting 400 lines of ERP markup into a UserControl, and a host view model holding one SelectedTabIndex

decisions.decision: Four stored procedures return per-day grain and C# does the daily, weekly and monthly bucketing
decisions.why: One fetch serves all three periods, so a period switch costs nothing and cannot disagree with itself, and the date arithmetic lives in one helper instead of four procedures
decisions.rejected: Passing a period into SQL and re-querying on every switch, or returning raw receipt rows and aggregating everything client side

decisions.decision: No new table, view, function or trigger; every total reads columns already on receiving_history
decisions.why: FR-031 and FR-032 permit new objects, they do not require them, and a generated view would add a layer without removing work
decisions.rejected: A generated totals view, or a summary table which would need a refresh and could go stale

decisions.decision: A load is COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(load_id, load_guid, id)); labels are COUNT(*); the missing-load-number count is disclosed beside them
decisions.why: label_number is written from the same session counter as load_number and load_id is fresh per row, so one completed receipt is one load and one label today; counting DISTINCT load_number would merge unrelated loads across sessions
decisions.rejected: Counting DISTINCT load_number, or reporting one receipts figure and dropping the load count

decisions.decision: One static Translation_ReceivingAnalyticsCategory owns both category vocabularies and the mapping; the app procedures pass part_type through untranslated
decisions.why: FR-027 wants one place, and today the ERP vocabulary exists three times over; keeping the app names out of SQL means the vocabulary has one home
decisions.rejected: A MySQL view holding the translation, which can only ever cover half of a cross-database mapping, or re-deriving app categories in SQL and duplicating the Model_ReceivingLoad rule

decisions.decision: Quantity sums COALESCE(weight_quantity, quantity) within one unit, and a blank unit becomes EA in C#
decisions.why: weight_quantity is the number the operator typed and quantity is that same number rounded; converting the blank unit in one C# helper keeps the pinned string in one place
decisions.rejected: Summing quantity alone, which discards the operator's decimals, or coalescing the unit inside each of four procedures

decisions.decision: The comparison reuses the existing Infor Visual query with identical bounds and all five scopes, and its inherited limits are documented rather than corrected
decisions.why: FR-002 and FR-033 forbid changing the ERP path, and the panel can only claim what it really compares: app labels against ERP receipt lines counted as the ERP counts them
decisions.rejected: A second ERP query tuned to match the app, which would drift and be the one nobody checks, and counting ERP quantities instead of lines

decisions.decision: Four panels in a 2x2 grid using the existing LiveCharts CartesianChart
decisions.why: Each quadrant is roughly 700x380 before headers, which holds two charts side by side but not two stacked, and LiveCharts is already referenced and used by this page
decisions.rejected: Adding a second charting library, pie or donut charts for the mix, or a scrolling page with larger charts against FR-006

decisions.decision: The four app reads run concurrently and any failure fails that dataset; the ERP comparison is a separate call whose failure is reported on its own panel
decisions.why: SC-004 needs four panels inside three seconds, and a half-loaded dataset of three agreeing panels plus one silently missing is exactly the lie this tab exists to catch
decisions.rejected: Sequential reads, or failing the whole tab when the ERP server is unreachable

decisions.decision: No is_reprint predicate on receiving_history
decisions.why: The flag marks a row re-queued for a reprint, and the completion procedure skips the insert for re-queued rows, so a reprint never creates a second history row; filtering it would delete real work
decisions.rejected: Excluding is_reprint = 1, which looks right and would undercount

decisions.decision: The app side of the category mix is quantity in the selected unit summed per ERP category
decisions.why: The activity rows carry per-category quantity but only per-day label totals, and the view model owns the unit choice, so summing label totals per category would count the labels of one day once per category row
decisions.rejected: Counting activity rows or per-day label totals per category

decisions.decision: The ERP per-category line counts travel on the comparison result as ErpCategoryTotals
decisions.why: The comparison carried only coverage points, so the view model had no ERP detail to build the ERP split from; the counts come from the ERP read already made, on identical bounds
decisions.rejected: Computing both shares in the service, which loses the unit-scoped app side, or a second ERP read

decisions.decision: The on-time target is read through IService_ShipRecToolsSettings on every load and an absent target shows a plain n/a
decisions.why: No percentage is hard-coded; a target with no dated receipts must not be coloured green as though it passed
decisions.rejected: A 95 default constant in the view model, and colouring the absent figure off IsOnTimeBelowTarget

decisions.decision: The five leading suppliers are ranked individually and the tail becomes one Other suppliers entry
decisions.why: The cumulative share only reaches one hundred per cent when the remainder is present
decisions.rejected: Ranking every supplier and leaving the chart to scroll

decisions.decision: Both coverage lines are drawn over the union of their dates, at zero where one side recorded nothing
decisions.why: The reader compares the same days on both lines, and a date only one system recorded is a real difference rather than a gap
decisions.rejected: Drawing each line over its own dates

decisions.decision: Both halves of the category mix count receipts
decisions.why: Item 9 asks whether we classify material the way the ERP does, and a share of quantity against a share of receipt lines cannot answer that question
decisions.rejected: Keeping the app share on quantity and relabelling the panel

decisions.decision: A per-group receipt_count column on GetActivityByDay rather than another procedure
decisions.why: The panel already reads those rows, and load_count and label_count stay day totals that the activity panel depends on
decisions.rejected: A fifth stored procedure, or deriving the receipt count from the existing day totals

decisions.decision: The integration tests seed a far-future window and delete by part id prefix
decisions.why: The counts they assert are their own even on a shared test schema
decisions.rejected: Filtering existing history, which makes assertions depend on whatever the database holds

plan.summary: Planned the two-tab split with a new App Data read path of four stored procedures, a shared category translation, and a settings-held on-time target
plan.key_finding: In the app's data model one completed receipt row is one load and one label at the same time, because label_number is written from the same session counter as load_number, so the two panel figures agree by construction and the missing-load-number disclosure is what makes that readable rather than suspicious

specify.summary: Phases 4 to 6 built: the on-time panel with a target-coloured percentage, the supplier ranking with a remainder, and the app-versus-ERP coverage and mix panels.

approach: The page becomes a TabView whose first item wraps the untouched ERP markup and whose second hosts a new App Data control with its own view model. App Data reads MySQL through four new stored procedures in a new DAO and service, buckets the per-day rows in C# for daily, weekly and monthly views, and takes the ERP side of the comparison from the existing read-only Infor Visual query.

concerns.note: T038 assigns both category splits to the view model, but the comparison model carried no per-category ERP detail; a new ErpCategoryTotals field and a small service change were needed to build the ERP split.

The two mix shares measure different things: the app side is quantity in the selected unit, the ERP side is receipt lines. The panel states this, but the two splits are comparable in shape rather than in unit.

SC-001 was not measured. The App Data tab is a star-row grid with no ScrollViewer, so the panels are laid out to fit rather than to scroll, but the visual check at 1450x900 on the shop floor terminal has not been done.
SC-004 was not measured. A thirty day range under three seconds needs the shop floor terminal and real data; the ERP read runs concurrently by code.
SC-005 was not measured. No hand count of a hundred sampled receipts was performed against live data; the early, on-time and late boundary is covered by unit tests only.
SC-006 was not produced twice live from both tabs. Identity rests on both tabs calling the same ERP read with the same bounds and all five scopes, which the service test asserts.
SC-009 was not exercised interactively. Ten tab switches with filter changes remain a manual check; each tab owns its own view model, so cross-tab leakage is structurally absent.

39 pre-existing StoredProcedureInitialCoverageIntegrationTests fail when a live test connection string is supplied, because mtm_receiving_application_test is missing dunnage_specs and other objects. They early-return in the default run, which is why the 929-test baseline passes. Environmental and pre-existing, not caused by this change.
The four new procedures were deployed into mtm_receiving_application_test by hand so the integration tests could run. They still need the standard deployment to production.
